content:
The [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Build an XML sitemap from your page URLs — ready to submit to Google. Enter your page URLs (one per line) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Build an XML sitemap from a list of your page URLs: add optional last-modified dates, change frequencies and priorities, and copy or download the finished sitemap.xml. A sitemap tells search engines which pages exist on your site and how often they change, so new and updated pages get found faster. Everything runs in your browser; your URLs are never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the XML Sitemap Generator

Start by typing or pasting your page URLs (one per line). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your page URLs, one per line.
2. Set last-modified dates, change frequency and priority where you know them (all optional).
3. Copy or download the sitemap.xml, upload it to your site's root, and submit it in Search Console.

## How it works

The [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What goes in a sitemap

Every page you want search engines to find, with its full address. Last-modified dates help crawlers spot updated pages; changefreq is a hint about how often a page changes; priority (0.0–1.0) says which pages matter most relative to each other. None of the three optional fields is required — a list of URLs alone is a valid sitemap.

## Sitemap limits

One sitemap holds up to 50,000 URLs and must stay under 50 MB uncompressed. Larger sites split their sitemaps and list them in a sitemap index file. If your site has more than a few hundred pages, generate the sitemap from your CMS or a crawler instead of typing URLs by hand.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Include only pages you want indexed — leave out admin, search and duplicate pages.
- Put the sitemap at your site's root and add its address to robots.txt.
- Submit it in Google Search Console and re-submit after big changes.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an XML sitemap?

A file listing a site's pages in a format search engines read, so they can find and crawl every page — especially new or rarely linked ones. Try it with your own numbers in the [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I need lastmod, changefreq and priority?

No. A sitemap with just URLs is valid. Last-modified dates are the most useful of the three; changefreq and priority are only hints. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### How many URLs can a sitemap hold?

Up to 50,000 URLs and 50 MB uncompressed. Bigger sites use several sitemaps listed in a sitemap index file. Try it with your own numbers in the [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

Yes. The XML Sitemap Generator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [XML Sitemap Generator](/xml-sitemap-generator) and start straight away.
